options.doc:
The maximum number of seconds that a scanning result will stay in the results cache. -1 disables the limit. 0 disables caching.

If this option is not set, the default is 10.

options.name: virusfilter:quarantine directory mode
options.doc:
This is the octet mode for the quarantine directory and its sub-directories as they are created.

If this option is not set, the default is 0755 or S_IRUSR | S_IWUSR | S_IXUSR | S_IRGRP | S_IXGRP | S_IROTH | S_IXOTH.

Permissions must be such that all users can read and search. I.E. don't mess with this unless you really know what you are doing.

options.name: virusfilter:block suspected file
options.doc:
With this option on, suspected malware will be blocked as well. Only the fsavscanner supports this option.

If this option is not set, the default is false.

vfs_modules.doc:
This is a set of various Samba VFS modules to scan and filter virus files on Samba file services with an anti-virus scanner.

This module is stackable.

vfs_modules.name: widelinks
vfs_modules.summary: make a Samba share ignore filesystem symbolic links inside a share
vfs_modules.doc:
This VFS module is part of the samba(7) suite.

The vfs_widelinks VFS module hides the existence of symbolic links in the filesystem inside a share. It is used in Samba version 4.13 and above to implement the smb.conf"wide links = yes" functionality that used to be inside the core smbd code. The module should not be loaded explicitly by smb.conf as part of the "vfs objects =" parameter, but is loaded implicitly when "wide links = yes" is enabled. This is to prevent existing smb.conf files from having to be modified to keep the existing insecure "wide links" functionality on a share.

Please note that "wide links = yes" functionality is a deliberately insecure option, and should never be used in Samba installations. On Linux, bind mounts can be used instead to implement anything "wide links = yes" can enable. This module has been created to provide backwards compatibility with existing users of "wide links = yes" installations, but this use cannot be recommended and is not endorsed by the Samba developers.

Note that this implicit loading may become explicit in a later Samba release, and administrators wishing to keep the insecure "wide links" functionality may have to add this module into their "vfs objects =" module list. The Samba project release notes and this manpage will be updated to reflect this when this change is made.

This module is stackable.

vfs_modules.name: worm
vfs_modules.summary: disallows writes for older file

options.name: worm:grace_period
options.doc: Period in seconds which defines the time how long the write access should be handled by the normal access controls. After this grace period the file or directory becomes read only.

vfs_modules.doc:
This VFS module is part of the samba(7) suite.

The vfs_worm module controls the writability of files and folders depending on their change time and a adjustable grace period.

If the change time of a file or directory is older than the specified grace period, the write access will be denied, independent of further access controls (e.g. by the filesystem).

In the case that the grace period is not exceed, the worm module will not impact any access controls.

vfs_modules.name: xattr_tdb
vfs_modules.summary: Save Extended Attributes (EAs) in a tdb file

options.name: xattr_tdb:file
options.doc: Name of the tdb file the EAs are stored in. If this option is not set, the default filename xattr.tdb is used.

vfs_modules.doc:
This VFS module is part of the samba(7) suite.

The vfs_xattr_tdb VFS module stores Extended Attributes (EAs) in a tdb file. This enables the usage of Extended Attributes on OS and filesystems which do not support Extended Attributes by themselves.

This module is stackable.

substitutions.name: %U
substitutions.doc: session username (the username that the client wanted, not necessarily the same as the one they got).

substitutions.name: %G
substitutions.doc: primary group name of %U.

substitutions.name: %h
substitutions.doc: the Internet hostname that Samba is running on.

substitutions.name: %m
substitutions.doc:
the NetBIOS name of the client machine (very useful).

This parameter is not available when Samba listens on port 445, as clients no longer send this information. If you use this macro in an include statement on a domain that has a Samba domain controller be sure to set in the [global] section server smb transports = 139. This will cause Samba to not listen on port 445 and will permit include functionality to function as it did with Samba 2.x.

substitutions.name: %L
substitutions.doc: the NetBIOS name of the server. This allows you to change your config based on what the client calls you. Your server can have a “dual personality”.

substitutions.name: %M
substitutions.doc: the Internet name of the client machine.

substitutions.name: %R
substitutions.doc: the selected protocol level after protocol negotiation. It can be one of CORE, COREPLUS, LANMAN1, LANMAN2, NT1, SMB2_02, SMB2_10, SMB3_00, SMB3_02, SMB3_11 or SMB2_FF.

substitutions.name: %d
substitutions.doc: the process id of the current server process.

substitutions.name: %a
substitutions.doc: The architecture of the remote machine. It currently recognizes Samba (Samba), the Linux CIFS file system (CIFSFS), OS/2, (OS2), Mac OS X (OSX), Windows for Workgroups (WfWg), Windows 9x/ME (Win95), Windows NT (WinNT), Windows 2000 (Win2K), Windows XP (WinXP), Windows XP 64-bit(WinXP64), Windows 2003 including 2003R2 (Win2K3), and Windows Vista (Vista). Anything else will be known as UNKNOWN.

substitutions.name: %I
substitutions.doc:
the IP address of the client machine.

Before 4.0.0 it could contain IPv4 mapped IPv6 addresses, now it only contains IPv4 or IPv6 addresses.

substitutions.name: %J
substitutions.doc: the IP address of the client machine, colons/dots replaced by underscores.

substitutions.name: %i
substitutions.doc:
the local IP address to which a client connected.

Before 4.0.0 it could contain IPv4 mapped IPv6 addresses, now it only contains IPv4 or IPv6 addresses.

substitutions.name: %j
substitutions.doc: the local IP address to which a client connected, colons/dots replaced by underscores.

substitutions.name: %T
substitutions.doc: the current date and time.

substitutions.name: %t
substitutions.doc: the current date and time in a minimal format without colons (YYYYYmmdd_HHMMSS).

substitutions.name: %D
substitutions.doc: name of the domain or workgroup of the current user.

substitutions.name: %w
substitutions.doc: the winbind separator.

substitutions.name: %$(envvar)
substitutions.doc: the value of the environment variable envar.

substitutions.name: %S
substitutions.doc: the name of the current service, if any.

substitutions.name: %P
substitutions.doc: the root directory of the current service, if any.

substitutions.name: %u
substitutions.doc: username of the current service, if any.

substitutions.name: %g
substitutions.doc: primary group name of %u.

substitutions.name: %H
substitutions.doc: the home directory of the user given by %u.

substitutions.name: %N
substitutions.doc: This value is the same as %L.
